title: Open Door Contract Limit per Customer (Entry & Patio Door Contracts)
content:
A customer may hold several Entry & Patio Door Contracts over time, but no more than 2 may be open at the same time. An open door contract is one whose status is signed, measured, ordered or installed; closed and cancelled door contracts do not count.

**Rule.** A new door contract may be signed only when the customer's count of open door contracts is below the cap of 2. When the cap is already reached, an additional door is added to an open door contract by change order before its order release, or the new contract waits until an open door contract closes. Window contracts are a separate product line and never count toward this cap.

**Basis of the count.** The count is taken from the company's contract records at the moment of handling, across every door contract held under the same customer, by contract status. It is not taken from the customer's own account of what they hold.

## Status of each door contract and whether it counts

| Door contract status | Counts as open |
|---|---|
| Signed | Yes |
| Measured | Yes |
| Ordered | Yes |
| Installed | Yes |
| Closed | No |
| Cancelled | No |

## Count of open door contracts and a new signing

| Open door contracts on record | New door contract may be signed |
|---|---|
| 0 | Yes |
| 1 | Yes |
| 2 | No: the cap of 2 is reached |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical holdings)

- A customer holding one installed door contract and one cancelled door contract has 1 open door contract, so a new door contract may be signed.
- A customer holding one measured door contract and one ordered door contract has 2 open door contracts; a new door contract is not signed. An additional door is instead added by change order to an open door contract before its order release, or the new contract waits until an open door contract closes.
- A customer holding two open door contracts and three Window Replacement Contracts still has 2 open door contracts for this purpose; the window contracts are not counted.
